extracted.intended_audience: users of FederalRegister.gov (members of the public, researchers, legal/regulatory stakeholders, and commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using the FederalRegister.gov website: explains legal status of the site, search and navigation behavior, document features (links, utility bar, public inspection), subscription/sharing options, comment submission limitations, and how to compute effective dates and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status of FederalRegister.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a “Web 2.0” version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register, and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO’s govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The XML-based Federal Register on FederalRegister.gov is an unofficial informational resource until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register (ACFR) issues a regulation granting it official legal status. While efforts have been made to display material accurately and consistently with the official SGML-based PDF version on govinfo.gov, those relying on it for legal research should verify results against an official edition. Until ACFR grants official status, the XML rendition does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking to the official PDF on govinfo.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document posted on the site includes a link to the corresponding official PDF file on govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should follow the link to the official govinfo.gov PDF when they need the official/legal edition; FederalRegister.gov provides the XML/HTML rendition and a link for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader Aids are informal user guidance (not published in the Federal Register)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader Aids help people use FederalRegister.gov and understand the federal rulemaking process. Reader Aids information is not published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reader Aids are explanatory material provided on the website to assist users; they do not constitute regulatory text or official Federal Register content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of documents into topical sections
rubrics_metrics.description: We organize published Federal Register documents into six sections, similar to a web journal (Money, Environment, World, Science & Technology, Business & Industry, and Health & Public Welfare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site groups documents by these broad themes to cover a majority of published documents and to make browsing easier; featured articles are shown in these sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document text features — activation of agency-included links
rubrics_metrics.description: Active Links: When an agency has included links as part of the document text, we activate those links using the text in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links may not work if the link in the published document contained an error or if the target website is no longer at that location. The site also uses automated legal links (where available) to connect to related legal materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document utility bar and sidebar features
rubrics_metrics.description: Document Utility Bar: The utility bar runs along the left side of the document and scrolls with you down the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the utility bar users can access the Public Inspection version and the official electronic format of the published document using the 2 bottom icons, print using the printer icon, and access sharing functions (email, etc.). The sidebar also provides links for sharing documents and subscription management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the Public Inspection page
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Inspection web page on FederalRegister.gov offers a preview of documents scheduled to appear in the next day’s Federal Register issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Public Inspection page may also include documents scheduled for later issues at the request of the issuing agency, giving the public access to important or complex documents before they publish in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting restrictions — site feedback is not for rulemaking comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Our “Site Feedback” tool and Federal Register email addresses are only intended for users to submit technical questions and comments on the functionality of the FederalRegister.gov website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools cannot be used to submit comments on rulemaking actions or to petition agencies on public policy issues. The site operators have no authority or ability to process comments on rulemaking; users must submit comments via the methods specified in the agency’s notice (e.g., regulations.gov or the agency’s comment portal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search tips — basic and advanced search behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: This site has a basic search tool and an advanced search. The basic search box appears in the main navigation at the top every page. The 'Search' pull-down tab in the main navigation shows various search options: Document Search: You can search by citation (for example, enter: ’75 FR 12345′ or ’75 Fed. Reg. 12345′).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of searchable inputs include FR citations (e.g., 88 FR 382), docket numbers, agency names (e.g., USDA), dates (e.g., 09/05/24), document types (e.g., RULE), CFR parts (e.g., 0503-AA39), and subject tags (e.g., SORN). Choosing an item from full text search results will bring you to those results; pressing enter in the search box will also bring you to search results. Choosing an item from suggestions will bring you directly to the content. See the Search & Navigation guide for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription and sharing options
rubrics_metrics.description: The site includes tools for sharing documents with associates and communities via email notification subscriptions, RSS feeds, and Twitter and Facebook social networking applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You also can send emails of Federal Register documents to associates and communities on a one-time basis. The sidebar on the left side of the document provides links to many of these subscription and sharing options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Effective Dates & Time Periods — computing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: This table is used by the Office of the Federal Register to compute certain dates, such as effective dates and comment deadlines, which appear in agency documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In computing these dates, the day after publication is counted as the first day. When a date falls on a weekend or holiday, the next Federal (business) day is used. (Table maintained/updated; example date rules shown as of June 2022.)
